description: The voice scope of Multi-brand: its answers, its usage rules and the semantic tokens it owns. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

answers.question: voice.roles
answers.why: Each brand has headlines on top of shared UI copy.

answers.question: voice.count
answers.why: A shared core, with a tone per brand.

answers.question: voice.definition
answers.why: Errors and confirmations are shared; brand tone sits on top.

answers.question: voice.values
answers.why: The shared core is plain and direct.

answers.question: voice.lands
answers.why: Brand tone shows in headlines and buttons.

usage.use: A shared verb; the brand may choose the headline verb
usage.why: Shared labels keep the account area the same in every brand.

usage.use: Shared across brands: plain and specific
usage.why: Errors read the same in every brand, so support can help anyone.
usage.example: Your card was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.

usage.use: Brand tone allowed: Aster calm, Birch friendly, Coral upbeat
usage.not: The same flat line in every brand
usage.why: Success is a safe moment for brand tone.
usage.example: Aster: Your plan is active. · Birch: You're all set! · Coral: Let's go, your plan is live.

usage.why: The structure is the shared core; words carry the brand.
usage.example: No orders yet. Your first order will appear here.

usage.use: Shared across brands: plain and specific
usage.not: Brand tone when something is lost
usage.why: Loss is never the moment for personality.
usage.example: Cancel your plan? It stays active until the end of the month.

usage.use: Brand tone in the first headline only
usage.why: One headline carries the brand; the rest stays shared.
usage.example: Birch: Hi! Let's set up your plan.

content.$description: Voice tokens: the words components use for common actions. Text, not CSS.

commit.$description: The label of the action that completes a task.

cancel.$description: The label of the way out next to the main action.

destroy.$description: The label of an action that deletes data.

retry.$description: The label that repeats a failed action.

empty-action.$description: The label of the action in an empty state.
